verses.zh: 耶和华的使者从吉甲上到波金，对以色列人说：「我使你们从埃及上来，领你们到我向你们列祖起誓应许之地。我又说：『我永不废弃与你们所立的约。
verses.en: The angel of the Lord[NOTE:1] went up from Gilgal to Bokim. He said, “I brought you up from Egypt and led you into the land I had solemnly promised to give to your ancestors.[NOTE:2] I said, ‘I will never break my covenant with you,
notes: Heb “the land that I had sworn to your fathers.”
verses.commentary:
2:1 "the angel of the Lord" Notice this angel speaks as if YHWH Himself (i.e., a
theophany).

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE Lord

- SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

▣ "came up from Gilgal" Notice the angel is depicted as moving (i.e., "came up"), following the same route
as Joshua's initial invasion. Gilgal was the first campsite of Israel in the Promised Land (cf. Jos. 4:19-20).

Gilgal (BDB 166 II) means "rolling" and is defined in Jos. 5:9 ("today I have rolled away the reproach
of Egypt from you").

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

▣ "to Bochim" The exact site is uncertain but it probably is close to Gilgal. The name means "weepers"
(BDB 114, cf. Jdgs. 2:5).

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 513, asserts that Bochim is really Bethel because of

- connection of Bethel to weeping (cf. Jdgs. 20:26; 21:2)

- the golden calf worship recorded in 1 Kgs. 12:25-30

Other reasons are:

- an "oak of weeping" is mentioned close to Bethel in Gen. 35:8

- the LXX specifically includes the name "and to Bethel"

- Bethel was the site of an altar, cf. Jdgs. 2:5; 20:27

▣ "I brought you up out of Egypt" This very phrase begins the "Ten Commandments" (cf. Exod. 20:2). This
divine act was the fulfillment of Gen. 15:12-21.

▣ "and led you into the land which I have sworn to your fathers" This first promise was given to Abraham in
Gen. 12:1-3 (cf. Deut. 1:8, 35; 6:10, 18, 23; 7:13; 8:1; 11:9, 21; 19:8; 26:3, 15; 28:11; 30:20; 31:23).

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "I will never break My covenant with you" This could refer to

- YHWH's statement in Gen. 3:1

- YHWH's promise to the Patriarchs

YHWH has a plan for redeeming all humanity which involved Abraham and his seed. However, their covenant
was conditional on human response and faithfulness. Judges highlights Israel's faithlessness (i.e., disobedience in relation to the Canaanite
population's removal and later Israel's adoption of their fertility worship, cf. Jdgs. 2:20-3:7). Israel's disobedience had consequences.

- YHWH stopped helping the individual tribes conquer their land allotment (Jos. 23:4-5, 23)

- YHWH sent oppressors (Jdgs. 2:3, 21)

The mercy and long term purpose of YHWH for Israel is also seen in that He sent deliverers (cf. Jdgs. 2:16)! It is
ultimately seen in the "New Covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34 (described in Ezek. 36:22-36).

Just one final comment. The Assyrian and Babylonian exiles were a reversal of the land promise of the
Abrahamic covenant. As YHWH removed the wicked Canaanites (cf. Gen. 15:12-21), so too, He removed the wicked
descendants of Abraham from Canaan.

The good news is He will bring them back (cf. Isa. 44:28; 45:1)! There is a long term purpose for Israel
(i.e., the Messiah).

- SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL
REDEMPTIVE PLAN

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

- SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

- SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ The MT concludes Jdgs. 2:2 with 'olam. This word has a wide semantic field and must be interpreted
in context.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 你们也不可与这地的居民立约，要拆毁他们的祭坛。你们竟没有听从我的话！为何这样行呢？』
verses.en: but you must not make an agreement with the people who live in this land. You should tear down the altars where they worship.’[NOTE:1] But you have disobeyed me.[NOTE:2] Why would you do such a thing?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “their altars.”
Heb “you have not listened to my voice.”
Heb “What is this you have done?”
verses.commentary:
2:2 "you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land" Judges 1:22-33 documents this disobedience.
Instead of removing or destroying the Canaanite population, they used them for "forced labor" (cf. Jdgs. 1:28, 30, 33, 35).

▣ "you shall tear down their altars" These were high places of Canaanite fertility worship.

- a large raised, upright stone, phallic stone, symbolizing the male god, Ba'al (cf. Exod. 23:24; 34:13)

- tall wooden stake representing the female goddess, Astarte, Asherah (cf. Exod. 34:13; similar mythology to the
Babylonian Ishtar)

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

▣ "But you have not obeyed Me; what is this you have done?" This, like Jdgs. 2:11-23, is an overview of the
period of the Judges; cycles of disobedience, mercy, deliverance, and renewed disobedience.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 因此我又说：『我必不将他们从你们面前赶出；他们必作你们肋下的荆棘。他们的　神必作你们的网罗。』」
verses.en: At that time I also warned you,[NOTE:1] ‘If you disobey,[NOTE:2] I will not drive out the Canaanites[NOTE:3] before you. They will ensnare you[NOTE:4] and their gods will lure you away.’”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “And I also said.” The use of the perfect tense here suggests that the messenger is recalling an earlier statement (see Josh 23:12-13). However, some translate, “And I also say,” understanding the following words as an announcement of judgment upon those gathered at Bokim.
The words “If you disobey” are supplied in the translation for clarity. See Josh 23:12-13.
Heb “them”; the referent (the Canaanites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The meaning of the Hebrew word צִדִּים (tsiddim) is uncertain in this context. It may be related to an Akkadian cognate meaning “snare.” If so, a more literal translation would be “they will become snares to you” (cf. NIV11 “traps”). Normally the term in question means “sides,” but this makes no sense here. On the basis of Num 33:55 some suggest the word for “thorns” has been accidentally omitted. If this word is added, the text would read, “they will become [thorns] in your sides” (cf. NASB, NIV84, NLT).
Heb “their gods will become a snare to you.”
verses.commentary:
2:3 This imagery comes from Num. 33:55 and Jos. 23:13. There were consequences to disobedience, terrible
consequences. The great promises of YHWH's presence and blessing of Israel are balanced with warnings for disobedience
(cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28). Israel must choose (cf. Deuteronomy 30)!

▣ "as thorns in your sides" The MT of Num. 33:55 has "thorns" (BDB 856), which seems to have
dropped out of the text of Jdgs. 2:3. The LXX translates MT's "sides" (BDB 841) as

- obstacle, LXX Alexandrinus

- oppression, LXX Vaticanus

- oppressors or adversaries (Targums, NJB, based on the "r" and "d" confusion in the two Hebrew roots)

The UBS Text Project, p. 74, suggests it is some type of hunting instrument; based on an Akkadian cognate
for "snare" (NET Bible, p. 429, #8).

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者向以色列众人说这话的时候，百姓就放声而哭；
verses.en: When the angel of the Lord finished speaking these words to all the Israelites, the people wept loudly.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “lifted their voices and wept.”
verses.commentary:
2:4-5 Apparently the coming of the Angel of the Lord was after Israel had already sinned. She tried to offer
a sacrifice but it was too late.

2:4 "they wept" This may be an example of "superficial repentance," cf. Num. 25:6; Jdsg. 20:33; 21:2; Ps. 51:17;
Joel 2:12-14, 17-19.

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE IN THE OT

verses.zh: 于是给那地方起名叫波金（就是哭的意思）。众人在那里向耶和华献祭。
verses.en: They named that place Bokim[NOTE:1] and offered sacrifices to the Lord there.
notes: Bokim means “weeping ones” and is derived from the Hebrew verb בָּכָא (bakhaʾ, “to weep”).

verses.zh: 从前约书亚打发以色列百姓去的时候，他们各归自己的地业，占据地土。
verses.en: When Joshua dismissed[NOTE:1] the people, the Israelites went to their allotted portions of territory,[NOTE:2] intending to take possession of the land.
notes: Or “sent away.”
Heb “the Israelites went each to his inheritance.”
verses.commentary: 2:6-10 This is a flashback to the events surrounding Joshua's death and burial (cf. Jos. 24:29-31).

verses.zh: 约书亚在世和约书亚死后，那些见耶和华为以色列人所行大事的长老还在的时候，百姓都事奉耶和华。
verses.en: The people worshiped[NOTE:1] the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and as long as the elderly men[NOTE:2] who outlived him remained alive. These men had witnessed[NOTE:3] all the great things the Lord had done for Israel.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “served”; or “followed.”
Or perhaps “elders,” which could be interpreted to mean “leaders.”
Heb “all the days of Joshua and all the days of the old men who outlived him, who had seen.”
Heb “the great work of the Lord which he had done for Israel.”
verses.commentary:
2:7 The generation that experienced YHWH's actions remained faithful but the future generations, who only heard
about them, disobeyed (cf. Jdgs. 2:10).

verses.zh: 耶和华的仆人、嫩的儿子约书亚，正一百一十岁就死了。
verses.en: Joshua son of Nun, the Lord’s servant, died at the age of 110.
verses.commentary:
2:8 "the servant of the Lord" This was an honorific title given to Joshua only after his
death (cf. Jos. 24:29).

- SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

▣ "the age of one hundred and ten" In Egyptian culture, this was the ideal age (cf. Gen. 50:22,26).

It is uncertain why the people lived so long in the early part of Genesis. There are only theories.

There has been much discussion about the length of human life before and immediately after the great
flood (i.e., the antediluvian period). Some have asserted that

- it is figurative

- they calculated years differently

- sin had simply not pervaded the earth as it has today

- the advanced ages were used to show honor for previous leaders as in the Sumerian lists of ten pre-flood kings. In that
list, the kings before the flood lived much longer than the kings after the flood, much like the genealogies of the Bible.

verses.zh: 以色列人将他葬在他地业的境内，就是在以法莲山地的亭拿・希烈，在迦实山的北边。
verses.en: The people[NOTE:1] buried him in his allotted land[NOTE:2] in Timnath Heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “in the territory of his inheritance.”
verses.commentary:
2:9 "Timnath-heres" This name (BDB 584) means "territory of the Sun." Sun worship is also implied in Judges 1.

- Beth-shemesh, Jdgs. 1:33

- Mount Heres, Jdgs. 1:35

This pagan association caused the Israelites to change the name of the location of Joshua's burial
(cf. Jos. 19:50; 24:30).

▣ "in the hill country of Ephraim" Joshua was from the tribe of Ephraim.

verses.zh: 那世代的人也都归了自己的列祖。后来有别的世代兴起，不知道耶和华，也不知道耶和华为以色列人所行的事。
verses.en: That entire generation passed away;[NOTE:1] a new generation grew up[NOTE:2] that had not personally experienced the Lord’s presence or seen what he had done for Israel.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “All that generation were gathered to their fathers.”
Heb “arose after them.”
Heb “that did not know the Lord or the work which he had done for Israel.” The expressions “personally experienced” and “seen” are interpretive.
verses.commentary:
2:10 "All that generation also were gathered to their fathers" This phrase, like "sleep," is a euphemism for death.
In the ANE, when possible, families were buried in close proximity (cf. Gen. 15:15; 25:8; 47:30).

The other common idiom was "slept with their fathers" (cf. 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Kgs. 1:21; 2:10; 11:43, etc.).

See NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 470-471, 4. C.

Several family tombs are mentioned in the OT.

- the Patriarchs' ‒ Gen. 49:29, 31; 50:13

- Joshua's ‒ Jos. 24:30; Jdgs. 2:9

- Joseph's ‒ Jos. 24:32

▣ "another generation after them who did not know the Lord" The term "know"
(BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT) is not used here of general knowledge about YHWH, His actions
or His commands, but the fact that this new generation did not have a faith relationship with Him.

Biblical faith is only one generation away from extinction if parents and the community of faith fail to pass
on, not just facts about God, but an intimate, daily, obedient faith relationship with Him (cf. Deut. 6:4-9)!

- SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

verses.zh: 以色列人行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，去事奉诸巴力，
verses.en: The Israelites did evil before[NOTE:1] the Lord by worshiping[NOTE:2] the Baals.
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”
Or “serving”; or “following.”
verses.commentary:
2:11 "Baals" Fertility worship was evil (cf. Deut. 4:25; 9:18; 17:2; 22:19; Jdgs. 3:7, 12; 4:1; 6:1; 10:6; 13:1).

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

verses.zh: 离弃了领他们出埃及地的耶和华―他们列祖的　神，去叩拜别神，就是四围列国的神，惹耶和华发怒；
verses.en: They abandoned the Lord God of their ancestors[NOTE:1] who brought them out of the land of Egypt. They followed other gods—the gods of the nations who lived around them. They worshiped[NOTE:2] them and made the Lord angry.
notes: Or “fathers.”
Or “bowed before” (the same expression occurs in the following verse).
verses.commentary:
2:12 "they forsook the Lord" This VERB (BDB 736, KB 806, Qal
IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Jdgs. 2:13; 10:6,10,13) is used of forsaking

- YHWH ‒ Deut. 28:20; 31:16; Jdgs. 10:10; Jer. 1:16; Jon. 2:9

- His covenant ‒ Deut. 29:25; 1 Kgs. 19:10, 14

- His house (i.e., temple) ‒ 2 Chr. 24:18; Neh. 10:40

▣ "the God of their fathers" Notice Israel's Deity is called

- the angel of the Lord, Jdgs. 2:1

- YHWH, Jdgs. 2:12 (most often in this chapter)

- Eloah, Jdgs. 2:12

- SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY,
C. And D

▣ "they provoked the Lord to anger" This is anthropomorphic language (like
"the anger of the Lord burned," Jdgs. 2:14) to express the degree of displeasure that Israel's
God had with "other gods" (cf. Exod. 20:2-11; Deut. 5:6-15).

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

verses.zh: 并离弃耶和华，去事奉巴力和亚斯她录。
verses.en: They abandoned the Lord and worshiped Baal and the Ashtoreths.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Ashtoreths were local manifestations of the goddess Astarte.

verses.zh: 耶和华的怒气向以色列人发作，就把他们交在抢夺他们的人手中，又将他们付与四围仇敌的手中，甚至他们在仇敌面前再不能站立得住。
verses.en: The Lord was furious with Israel[NOTE:1] and handed them over to robbers who plundered them.[NOTE:2] He turned them over to[NOTE:3] their enemies who lived around them. They could no longer withstand their enemies’ attacks.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “The Lord’s anger burned [or “raged”] against Israel.”

The expression robbers who plundered them is a derogatory reference to the enemy nations, as the next line indicates.tn Heb “robbers who robbed them.” (The verb שָׁסָה [shasah] appears twice in the verse.)
Heb “sold them into the hand of.”
The word “attacks” is supplied in the translation both for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
2:14 "the hands of plunderers who plundered" This is a purposeful grammatical combination of

- BDB 1042, KB 1608, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- BDB 1042, KB 1608, Qal IMPERFECT with waw

▣ "He sold them into the hands of their enemies" This is an idiom (cf. Jdgs. 3:8; 4:2,9; 10:7; 1 Sam. 12:9)
for God allowing the Canaanites to defeat His people.

It is the antonym of the term "redeem" which means "to buy someone back."

- SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

- SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 他们无论往何处去，耶和华都以灾祸攻击他们，正如耶和华所说的话，又如耶和华向他们所起的誓；他们便极其困苦。
verses.en: Whenever they went out to fight,[NOTE:1] the Lord did them harm,[NOTE:2] just as he had warned and solemnly vowed he would do.[NOTE:3] They suffered greatly.[NOTE:4]
notes: The expression “to fight” is interpretive.
Heb “the Lord’s hand was against them for harm.”
Heb “just as he had said and just as he had sworn to them.”
Or “they experienced great distress.”
verses.commentary:
2:15 The Divine Warrior (i.e., holy war terminology) was now on the side of the enemy! Israel had ignored
Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28. Actions have consequences.

verses.zh: 耶和华兴起士师，士师就拯救他们脱离抢夺他们人的手。
verses.en: The Lord raised up leaders[NOTE:1] who delivered them from these robbers.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or more traditionally, “judges” (also in vv. 17, 18 [3x], 19). Since these figures carried out more than a judicial function, also serving as rulers and (in several instances) as military commanders, the translation uses the term “leaders.”
Heb “and they delivered them from the hand of the ones robbing them.”
verses.commentary:
2:16 However, the mercy of YHWH is seen in Jdgs. 2:16.

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 他们却不听从士师，竟随从叩拜别神，行了邪淫，速速地偏离他们列祖所行的道，不如他们列祖顺从耶和华的命令。
verses.en: But they did not obey[NOTE:1] their leaders. Instead they prostituted themselves to other gods and worshiped[NOTE:2] them. They quickly turned aside from the path[NOTE:3] their ancestors[NOTE:4] had walked. Their ancestors had obeyed the Lord’s commands, but they did not.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “did not listen to.”
Or “bowed before.”
Or “way [of life].”
Or “fathers.”
Heb “…walked, obeying the Lord’s commands. They did not do this.”
verses.commentary:
2:17 The terrible cycle of faith, faithlessness, and renewal occurred again and again.

▣ "played the harlot" This imagery is both figurative and literal (cf. Exod. 34:15-16; Lev. 17:7; 20:5;
Deut. 31:16; Jdgs. 8:27, 35; 1 Chr. 5:25; Ps. 73:27; 106:39).

▣ "They turned aside quickly from the way" There are two images here.

- The VERB (BDB 693, KB 747, Qal PERFECT) denotes an apostasy, cf.
Exod. 32:8; Deut. 9:12; 11:16; 17:11, 17; 1 Sam. 12:20; Ps. 14:3; Jer. 5:23; 32:40; Ezek. 6:9

- "The way" denotes God's will as a clearly marked, straight, level road. Do not turn to the right or left, cf. Jdgs. 2:22;
Deut. 5:32; Jos. 1:7; 2 Kgs. 22:2.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY
(aphistēmi)

▣ "commandments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

verses.zh: 耶和华为他们兴起士师，就与那士师同在。士师在世的一切日子，耶和华拯救他们脱离仇敌的手。他们因受欺压扰害，就哀声叹气，所以耶和华后悔了。
verses.en: When the Lord raised up leaders for them, the Lord was with each leader and delivered the people[NOTE:1] from their enemies while the leader remained alive. The Lord felt sorry for them[NOTE:2] when they cried out in agony because of what their harsh oppressors did to them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “them”; the referent (the people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The phrase “for them” is supplied in the translation for clarity.

Heb “the ones oppressing them and afflicting them.” The synonyms “oppressing” and “afflicting” are joined together in the translation as “harsh oppressors” to emphasize the cruel character of their enemies.
verses.commentary:
2:18 "the Lord was moved to pity by their groaning" This shows the basic character
of YHWH, "mercy."

The fact that God was affected by His people's prayers clearly demonstrates that prayer makes a real difference.

This terminology is the same as Exod. 2:24; 3:9; 6:5, relating to Israel's time in Egyptian bondage.

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

- SPECIAL TOPIC: EFFECTIVE PRAYER

verses.zh: 及至士师死后，他们就转去行恶，比他们列祖更甚，去事奉叩拜别神，总不断绝顽梗的恶行。
verses.en: When a leader died, the next generation[NOTE:1] would again[NOTE:2] act more wickedly than the previous one.[NOTE:3] They would follow after other gods, worshiping them[NOTE:4] and bowing down to them. They did not give up[NOTE:5] their practices or their stubborn ways.
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the next generation) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The verb שׁוּב (shuv, “to return; to turn”) is sometimes translated “turn back” here, but it is probably used in an adverbial sense, indicating that the main action (“act wickedly”) is being repeated.

Heb “their fathers.”sn The statement the next generation would again act more wickedly than the previous one must refer to the successive sinful generations after Joshua, not Joshua’s godly generation (cf. vv. 7, 17).
Or “serving [them]”; or “following [them].”
Or “drop.”
verses.commentary:
2:19 "their stubborn ways" Notice the character of Israel:

- "the stubbornness of this people" ‒ BDB 904, cf. Jdgs. 2:6, 7, 13, 24, 27

- "their wickedness" ‒ BDB 957, cf. Jer. 14:20; Ezek. 3:19; 33:12

- "their sin" ‒ BDB 308, cf. Exod. 32:30; Deut. 9:18; Ps. 32:5; 51:5; Pro. 5:22; 13:6; 14:34; 21:4; 24:9 (Deuteronomy
shares the vocabulary of the sages of Hebrew Wisdom Literature)

verses.zh: 于是耶和华的怒气向以色列人发作。他说：「因这民违背我吩咐他们列祖所守的约，不听从我的话，
verses.en: The Lord was furious with Israel.[NOTE:1] He said, “This nation[NOTE:2] has violated the terms of the covenant I made with their ancestors[NOTE:3] by disobeying me.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “The Lord’s anger burned [or “raged”] against Israel.”
Heb “Because this nation.”
Heb “my covenant which I commanded their fathers.”
Heb “and has not listened to my voice.” The expression “to not listen to [God’s] voice” is idiomatic here for disobeying him.
verses.commentary:
2:20-21 The faithlessness of Israel changed how YHWH treated them.

2:20 "covenant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

verses.zh: 所以约书亚死的时候所剩下的各族，我必不再从他们面前赶出，
verses.en: So I will no longer remove before them any of the nations that Joshua left unconquered when he died,

verses.zh: 为要藉此试验以色列人，看他们肯照他们列祖谨守遵行我的道不肯。」
verses.en: in order to test Israel.[NOTE:1][NOTE:2] I want to see[NOTE:3] whether or not the people[NOTE:4] will carefully walk in the path[NOTE:5] marked out by[NOTE:6] the Lord, as their ancestors[NOTE:7] were careful to do.”
notes: The Hebrew text of v. 22 simply begins with “to test.” Some subordinate this phrase to “I will no longer remove” (v. 21). In this case the Lord announces that he has now decided to leave these nations as a test for Israel. Another possibility is to subordinate “to test” to “He said” (v. 20; see B. Lindars, Judges 1-5, 111). In this case the statement recorded in vv. 20b-21 is the test in that it forces Israel to respond either positively (through repentance) or negatively to the Lord’s declaration. A third possibility is to subordinate “to test” to “left unconquered” (v. 21). In this case the Lord recalls that Joshua left these nations as a test. Israel has failed the test (v. 20), so the Lord announces that the punishment threatened earlier (Josh 23:12-13; see also Judg 2:3) will now be implemented. As B. G. Webb (Judges [JSOTSup], 115) observes, “The nations which were originally left as a test are now left as a punishment.” This view harmonizes v. 23, which explains that the Lord did not give all the nations to Joshua, with v. 22. (For a grammatical parallel, where the infinitive construct of נָסָה [nasah] is subordinated to the perfect of עָזַב [ʿazav], see 2 Chr 32:31.)
The Hebrew text includes the phrase “by them,” but this is somewhat redundant in English and has been omitted from the translation for stylistic reasons.
The words “I [i.e., the Lord] want to see” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

2:23 There is only one God. He, unlike the idols, can hear, act, show mercy, and direct history. In the OT there is
only one causality—God (cf. 2 Chr. 20:6; Eccl. 7:14; Isa. 14:24-27; 43:13; 45:7; 54:16; Jer. 18:11; Lam. 3:33-38; Amos 3:6).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Who is the angel of the Lord?

- What does "covenant" mean?

- Why do people in the early part of the OT live so long?

- Define the word "know" in Jdgs. 2:10.

- Who are Ba'al and Astarte?

- What does it mean "to play the harlot"?

- How does Jdgs. 2:18 demonstrate the mercy of YHWH?

- What does it mean that Israel was "stubborn"?

- Does God test nations and people?

- Why was YHWH with Joshua during the initial conquest but not with the northern tribes later?
